note: P6-04d0 division cost attribution. Profiling only, no code changes.
head: b6d568a9
conclusion: per quotient digit = 12.43 ns + 1.372 ns * nb, of which about 10.2 ns is __udivti3 -- exactly one compiler-rt 128-bit software division per digit. Fixed cost is roughly 57-68 ns. The six allocations are not the right starting point for the next cut.

wide_division_helper.how_established: nm plus a disassembly of divRemAbsNormalizedLong (one bl __udivti3, no __umodti3 in the binary at all -- the remainder is computed as numerator - qhat*v1), then gdb breakpoint counts. Not inferred from the u128 / u64 source expression.
wide_division_helper.memcpy_composition: two abs clones plus the u and v copies; these operands all have shift 0

axis_width_one_digit.reading: width from 2 to 32 limbs adds only 55.6 ns; that is the normalization copies and abs clones growing linearly

cost_model.nb_term: the multiply-subtract loop's nb limb iterations
cost_model.fixed_cost_ns: about 57-68: two abs clones, the u and v allocations and normalization copies, quotient and remainder construction, six allocations

direct_core_symbol_shares.caveat: init.gpa is libc malloc here, so the allocator share is overstated relative to the JS path, which uses the MemoryAccount slab

udivti3_absolute_ns.derivation: share times total divided by the digit count; not an independent timing

js_symbol_shares.note: the user-visible path; the picture differs from direct-core
js_symbol_shares.key_finding: for 8x4 the JS-level allocator share (26.3%) is LARGER than __udivti3 (13.7%); direct-core has it the other way round (20.9% vs 34.8%). Both are consistent: more quotient digits shift the balance toward the per-digit cost, and 8x4 has only five.

div_vs_mod.conclusion: the algorithm builds both results and discards one, which is exactly the P6-04d2b opportunity

decision.situation_A_per_digit_wide_division: holds for 5 or more quotient digits: 61% of 8x4 and 77% of 16x8, with __udivti3 alone at 30-35% of direct-core
decision.situation_B_allocations: holds at one quotient digit: 35-50% direct-core, about 26% at the JS level for the equal-width shapes
decision.recommendation: P6-04d1 first, because __udivti3 is the single largest addressable item and the only one that grows with size. Projected: if a reciprocal estimate cuts 10.2 ns per digit to about 2, 8x4 goes 146.3 -> 105 ns (3.20x -> about 2.3x, meeting the 2.5x gate) and 16x8 goes 272.7 -> 199 ns (1.60x -> about 1.17x).
decision.caveat: d1 alone will not put 8x4 inside 2x: at the JS level its allocator share is 26.3% against __udivti3's 13.7%, so d2a and d2b are necessary for that shape, and only the combination has a chance.
decision.agrees_with_qjs: Bellard qjs precomputes a reciprocal of the normalized divisor's top limb when na-nb >= 3 and then estimates each digit multiplicatively via udiv1norm, keeping double-limb division for short quotients. The threshold matches this attribution: 5x4 (two digits) is only 20% per-digit cost while 8x4 (five digits) is already 61%.

limits: only shift == 0 operands were measured, so the memcpy count of 4 is under that premise; with shift != 0 normalization goes through shiftLeftInto rather than @memcpy and that copy cost was not measured separately
the per-digit model is solved from two points (nb = 4 and nb = 8); linearity was not verified at nb = 2 or 16
the 10.2 / 9.2 ns per __udivti3 comes from a perf share times the total, not an independent timing
qhat correction and add-back counts were not measured this round; P6-04c's directed vectors prove they are reachable but the shipped code carries no counters
the direct-core and JS allocator shares are explained but were not normalized onto a common allocator for comparison
the equal-width shapes were not profiled at the JS level; only div_8x4, div_16x8 and mod_8x4 exist as JS cases

next_denominator.topology: 6 allocations and 4 memcpys per op, identical for div and mod
next_denominator.p6_04d1_gates: 8x4 and 16x8 at least 10% better with every combination same-direction; 2x2, 8x8 and 16x16 with no stable regression at or above 1%; no new regression on the four single-limb shapes including the already-waived mod-size-2x1 sentinel; correction and add-back results identical to P6-04c
